principle_text: When the seller has already lowered their price once, you should leverage concerns about the item's condition and used status to negotiate for a further reduction.
When the seller has already reached their lowest offer, creating urgency through a cash offer and emphasizing limited resources can lead to securing a better deal.
When the seller's item is described as being in very good condition, you should leverage perceived defects like sagging leather to negotiate a lower price effectively.

When the seller is willing to negotiate on price and terms, propose a middle-ground offer and introduce additional value requests to enhance the deal, leading to a more favorable outcome for the buyer.
When the buyer offers to self-arrange delivery, leverage this as a bargaining chip to prompt the seller to lower the price, even if the final offer is slightly higher.

When the seller has already reduced the price to $245 with delivery, avoid accepting the offer without further negotiation to prevent conceding leverage and potentially finalizing a less favorable deal.

When the seller offers a counterprice lower than the initial price, avoid increasing your offer significantly as it may lead to the seller demanding even higher prices, weakening your negotiation position.

When the seller shows willingness to negotiate and offers a slight discount, you should leverage this by proposing a counteroffer with added value, such as agreeing to pick up the item, to further lower the price and strengthen your position.

When the seller has already responded to a specific offer with a counteroffer and additional terms, avoid reiterating the same offer without acknowledging or addressing the seller's previous response.
When the seller's counteroffer is higher than the buyer's increased offer, avoid making concessions that weaken your leverage and push the price further away from your goal.
When the buyer accepts a price higher than their initial target, avoid finalizing the deal without further negotiation, as it weakens the buyer's leverage and may lead to a less favorable outcome.

When the seller emphasizes the luxury and quality of the item, avoid shifting focus away from price negotiation to non-essential details like delivery, as it weakens buyer leverage and allows the seller to maintain a higher price.

When the seller emphasizes the luxury and high quality of the item, avoid accepting a price significantly higher than your initial offer without further negotiation to maintain leverage and aim for a better deal.
